title: Hexalith.Conversations Release Waiver Schema
description: Structured specification for a named release-gate waiver record. A waiver makes an accepted risk explicit, owned, time-bound, and visible to release approvers and buyers where needed. Each waiver record must be traceable to a requirement or gate, list all affected stories, and carry a compensating control. This document is navigable by non-developer release approvers without requiring log or system access (NFR68).

fields.name: waiverId
fields.description: Stable bounded machine-readable identifier for the waiver. Must use only alphanumeric characters, hyphens, underscores, and dots. Maximum 128 characters. Example: waiver-story-5-4-named-waiver-process.

fields.name: owner
fields.description: Bounded identifier for the person or role accountable for this waiver. Must be a bounded safe-token. Example: release-engineer.

fields.name: approver
fields.validation: optional-safe-token; required-by-validator when isBlocker is true
fields.description: Optional bounded identifier for the approver who explicitly authorized this waiver. Null is valid at construction. The validator returns blocker-requires-approver when isBlocker is true and approver is null.

fields.name: affectedRequirementId
fields.description: The functional or non-functional requirement identifier this waiver covers. Example: FR85, NFR62.

fields.name: affectedGateId
fields.description: Optional release gate this waiver applies to. One of: tenant-isolation, audit-integrity, redaction-non-leakage, unsupported-schema-rejection, projection-rebuild-determinism, contract-compatibility, provider-portability. Null when the waiver covers a non-gate requirement.

fields.name: affectedStoryIds
fields.validation: non-empty; each element safe-token; no null elements
fields.description: Non-empty list of story key identifiers affected by this waiver. Each element must be a bounded safe-token. Example: ["5-4-support-named-waivers-for-release-gate-exceptions"].

fields.name: isBlocker
fields.description: True when this waiver covers an automatic release blocker under NFR62 (tenant isolation, audit integrity, redaction non-leakage, unsupported schema rejection, projection rebuild determinism, or contract breakage). Blocker waivers require an explicit approver and trigger buyer-facing acceptance checks when an affected gate is specified.

fields.name: risk
fields.description: Bounded human-readable description of the accepted risk. Maximum 512 characters. No control characters or protected identifiers.

fields.name: compensatingControl
fields.description: Bounded human-readable description of the compensating control that mitigates the accepted risk. Maximum 512 characters.

fields.name: expiryDateUtc
fields.validation: utc-timestamp; validator flags expired-waiver when past evaluatedAt
fields.description: UTC date-time when this waiver expires. Offset must be zero. The validator returns expired-waiver when ExpiryDateUtc is before the evaluatedAt point-in-time, regardless of lifecycle status.

fields.name: buyerImpact
fields.description: Bounded human-readable description of the impact on buyers or customers. Maximum 512 characters.

fields.name: buyerAcceptanceStatus
fields.validation: optional-safe-token; required-by-validator when isBlocker is true and affectedGateId is non-null
fields.description: Optional bounded token representing buyer acceptance status. Null means not customer-facing. Expected values: buyer-accepted, buyer-pending, not-applicable. The validator returns buyer-facing-missing-acceptance when isBlocker is true, affectedGateId is non-null, and buyerAcceptanceStatus is null.

fields.name: evidenceLinks
fields.validation: non-null; empty list allowed; each element safe-token
fields.description: Bounded list of safe-token evidence artifact handles supporting this waiver. Null list is not allowed; empty list is valid. Each element must be a bounded safe-token.

fields.name: reviewDateUtc
fields.validation: utc-timestamp; validator flags stale-review-date when past evaluatedAt
fields.description: UTC date-time for the next scheduled review of this waiver. Offset must be zero. The validator returns stale-review-date when ReviewDateUtc is before the evaluatedAt point-in-time.

fields.name: lifecycleStatus
fields.description: Current lifecycle state of the waiver. One of: active (currently valid and approved), expired (past ExpiryDateUtc; treated as a finding), rejected (explicitly denied by approver), superseded (replaced by a newer named waiver). Expired and superseded waivers are stale and may affect gate status.

fields.name: createdAtUtc
fields.description: UTC date-time when this waiver record was created. Offset must be zero.

validationRules.description: When isBlocker is true, the approver field must be non-null. A blocker waiver without an explicit named approver cannot be considered authoritative.
When ExpiryDateUtc is before the evaluatedAt point-in-time, the waiver is expired regardless of its lifecycleStatus value. An active waiver with a past expiry is still flagged as expired.
When ReviewDateUtc is before the evaluatedAt point-in-time, the waiver's review date is overdue. Stale review dates indicate the waiver may not reflect the current risk posture.

When isBlocker is true and affectedGateId is non-null (gate-specific blocker waiver), buyerAcceptanceStatus must be non-null. A buyer-facing blocker waiver without explicit acceptance status cannot be released without buyer visibility.

exampleRecord.risk: Named waiver process documentation may need iteration before GA
exampleRecord.compensatingControl: Waiver schema document and fixture provide navigable governance evidence for release approvers
exampleRecord.buyerImpact: Buyer can review named waivers through release evidence documents
